title: Platform Mechanics Atlas — Visibility, Persistence, Incentives and Social Memory
purpose: Model a platform as an active mediation system rather than a neutral container. Track how affordances, ranking, identity, monetization, moderation, archive rules and portability change what becomes visible, repeatable and memorable.

questions: Is identity persistent, pseudonymous, verified, portable or disposable?
What can be posted: text, video, live, thread, story, file, reaction, remix?
Follower graph, search, recommendation, trending, embedding, notifications or direct delivery?
Replies, quote-posts, duets, stitches, reactions, chat, moderation, collaboration?
Which signals influence ordering or recommendation?
Which parts are known versus opaque?
Ads, subscriptions, donations, revenue share, commerce, sponsorship, no direct monetization?
Rules, enforcement, appeals, account-level sanctions, object-level sanctions, age gates, regional restrictions?
Searchability, deletion, edit history, caching, clipping, download, external archives, API access?
Can users export identity, content, audience graph, subscriptions or archives?
Which metrics are public, private, estimated, sampled or unavailable?

core_mechanisms.mechanism: Only a subset of available objects is surfaced to a user.
Exposure produces interaction; interaction can affect further exposure.
core_mechanisms.boundary: Observed correlation between engagement and reach does not by itself reveal the full ranking algorithm.

core_mechanisms.mechanism: Material produced for one audience/time can circulate into another context.
Copies, clips, quotes, screenshots and external archives can outlive the original object or account.
A creator/community may depend on platform-owned discovery, payments, identity or audience access.
Rules and enforcement change which practices can persist.
Character limits, clip length, live chat, threading and remix tools change expression and interpretation.
Visible metrics become goals and status signals, changing behavior.

comparison_rule: Compare platforms by mechanisms and measurements, not by vague claims that one platform is 'more free', 'more toxic' or 'more viral'.

handoffs.information_ecology: Translate platform mechanics into attention, memory, repetition and correction dynamics.
handoffs.subculture_group_formation: Pass repeated interaction patterns only when there is evidence of identity, norms, roles or reproduction.
handoffs.witness_attestation: Preserve what was publicly witnessed without inferring private motive.
handoffs.below_observatory: Escalate abuse, harassment or illicit-network questions only with evidence-specific case records.

mechanism_cases.observation: Federated server-to-server delivery allows social objects and notifications to move across independently implemented services, changing the candidate/distribution topology from one platform-owned graph to a network of servers.
measurable_questions: How many independent servers/services participate in the path?
Can a receiving service render/reply to the object?
What happens to a thread when a source server disappears?
mechanism_cases.boundary: Federated delivery is not equivalent to global searchability, uniform moderation, guaranteed archival persistence or frictionless identity migration.

mechanism_cases.observation: AT Protocol separates persistent decentralized identity and signed user repositories from a specific hosting PDS, allowing provider changes without intending to change the user's underlying identity.
measurable_questions: Does the DID remain stable after provider migration?
Does the social graph resolve after migration?
Which application-specific state fails to migrate?
mechanism_cases.boundary: Protocol-level portability does not imply that every App View, labeler, recommendation history, moderation record or third-party application state is portable.

mechanism_cases.observation: YouTube distinguishes warnings, strikes, removals and restrictions; creators receive notices and many enforcement decisions can be appealed. Three Community Guidelines strikes within 90 days can terminate a channel.
measurable_questions: Was notice given and what reason was supplied?
Was an appeal available and was the action reversed?
Is the action represented in the transparency-report category being used?
mechanism_cases.boundary: Platform-published enforcement totals are scoped datasets. Some restrictions and other legal/privacy/copyright processes are outside particular Community Guidelines report measures.

mechanism_cases.observation: Users can create archives of data held across multiple Google products, demonstrating archive/data export as a distinct portability mechanism from live account or audience migration.
measurable_questions: Which product data categories are exportable?
Can another service import the export?
Which live identity, relationship or ranking state is absent from the archive?
mechanism_cases.boundary: An exportable archive improves user-held memory and exit resilience but does not recreate platform-native identity, audience relationships, recommendations or moderation state.

cross_file_chain.mechanics: This file asks what the platform/protocol does to identity, distribution, interaction, memory and measurement.
cross_file_chain.governance: platform-governance-portability-atlas asks who controls those mechanisms, what can be appealed/exported/migrated, and where dependency remains.
cross_file_chain.ecology: information-ecology-mechanics-atlas asks what those mechanisms do to attention, repetition, provenance, correction and collective memory.
cross_file_chain.repair: information-correction-memory-repair-atlas asks how changed status and corrections can propagate without erasing history.
